notes: Preuve : « How to Study for 10+ Hours » de @bdnf.milly (310,8 k vues, 24/09), même gabarit (couverture « How to / … / [IRM] / … », fond noir, 4 slides), sujet voisin de son « Habits that increase Intelligence » (142 k). Slide Sophia (3) : lire une leçon chaque soir comme un entraînement, le logo de Sophia au milieu (demande d'Adrien du 19/11 : le logo, jamais une capture). Faits vérifiés : hippocampe postérieur plus gros chez les chauffeurs de taxi londoniens, et d'autant plus qu'ils conduisent depuis longtemps (Maguire et al., PNAS 2000) ; trois mois de jonglage font grossir la matière grise des aires du mouvement visuel, qui régresse à l'arrêt (Draganski et al., Nature 2004) ; dormir peu après avoir appris retient mieux que rester éveillé le même temps (Gais, Lucas et Born, Learning & Memory 2006) ; se tester retient mieux à une semaine que relire (Roediger et Karpicke, Psychological Science 2006). Images : Seedream (images/), sans texte.

blocs.p: The brain physically adapts to what it is repeatedly asked to do. In a well-known study, London taxi drivers, who spend years memorizing thousands of streets, had a larger posterior hippocampus than other adults, and the difference grew with every year on the job.

Even three months of practicing a new skill is enough: adults who learned to juggle showed measurable growth in the grey matter of areas that process movement, and it faded once they stopped. Intelligence behaves like a muscle. It follows the training it receives.

The simplest way to train it is a small daily dose of new knowledge. One short lesson every evening, in history, science, philosophy or psychology, gives the brain something new to encode, connect and store, night after night.

Timing matters. Information learned shortly before sleep is consolidated during the night: in studies, people who slept soon after learning remembered more than people who stayed awake for the same amount of time.
I use Sophia for this: one short lesson before bed, every night, like a training session for the mind.

en.titre: Then Recall It In The Morning

blocs.p: Reading is only half of the training. Before looking at anything, try to recall what you learned the night before: the key idea, a date, a name. This is called retrieval practice, one of the most reliable effects in cognitive science.

Students who practiced recalling a text remembered far more of it a week later than students who simply reread it. Small reps, every night and every morning, for months: that is how the brain gets stronger.
